text:
San Jose Hockey Now called Will Smith's three-point night against Nashville the best game of his career and one of the best in the league this season. At 21, the fourth overall pick from 2023 keeps raising his own ceiling: eight goals and 19 points in 26 games, seven of those points on the power play, nearly 20 minutes a night.

If anything he's been unlucky. The goals trail the chances (8 on 9.5 expected), and the Sharks have scored 4.7 fewer goals than they deserve with him on the ice, which usually swings back. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why his looks are good ones: he gets 2.7 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, and those go in about 25% of the time. The Sharks' share of expected goals is 4.4 points better with him on. Our range projects 57 to 81 points. He's the second piece of the core, right behind Macklin Celebrini.
